section: Classification of basic industries - agro-based, mineral-based, forest-based, fuel-based and manpower-based

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an agro-based industry?
accepted.x: Cotton textiles are agro-based because cotton is an agricultural raw material. Cement, aluminium and iron and steel are mineral-based industries.
accepted.tq: Use the raw-material classification to distinguish agro-based from mineral-based industries.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Agro-based industry — Mega Food Park, Mallavalli
2. Mineral-based industry — Steel at Visakhapatnam
3. Forest-based industry — Paper from bamboo and eucalyptus
4. Animal-based industry — Leather in Nellore

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Mallavalli is associated with food processing, Visakhapatnam with steel, bamboo and eucalyptus with paper, and Nellore with leather.
accepted.tq: Check the raw material first and then verify the corresponding Indian or Andhra Pradesh example.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Industry type)
(a) Forest-based
(b) Marine-based
(c) Animal-based
(d) Agro-based

List-II (Example)
(i) Coastal aquaculture processing
(ii) Dairy
(iii) Pulp and paper
(iv) Sugar

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Forest-based industries include pulp and paper; marine-based industries include coastal aquaculture processing; dairy is animal-based; and sugar is agro-based.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes that assign a wrong raw material.

accepted.s: Why do agro-based industrial units generally locate near the source of raw materials?
o: Agricultural raw materials are usually heavier after processing
The raw materials may lose weight or perish during transport
Agricultural raw materials are always imported
Agro-based industries require no transport facilities
accepted.x: Agro-based units locate near raw materials because the materials may be perishable or may undergo weight loss during processing.
accepted.tq: Apply the location principle of weight loss and perishability.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Indian paper industry is correct?

1. India accounts for approximately 5% of world paper production.
2. Recycled fibre contributes about 71–75% of the raw material.
3. Wood pulp contributes about 21% of the raw material.
4. India’s per capita paper consumption is about 57 kg per year.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: India accounts for about 5% of world paper, recycled fibre contributes 71–75%, and wood pulp contributes about 21%. Indian per capita consumption is about 16 kg, not 57 kg; 57 kg is the world figure.
accepted.tq: Separate the Indian figure from the comparative world figure before selecting the statements.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is included among the wood-pulp sources used in paper manufacture?
accepted.x: Eucalyptus, poplar and subabul are mentioned as sources of wood pulp for paper manufacture.
accepted.tq: Identify the raw-material example rather than the mineral or fuel input.

accepted.s: Approximately how much water is required to produce one tonne of paper?
accepted.x: Paper production requires approximately 100–150 tonnes of water per tonne of paper.
accepted.tq: Use the range-based numerical clue and reject values outside the stated range.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the ownership pattern of the industry?
accepted.x: SAIL is a public-sector enterprise. RINL and HAL are also public-sector examples, while Amul is a cooperative enterprise.
accepted.tq: Use ownership identity to detect the wrongly assigned enterprise.
accepted.sec: By ownership - public, private, joint, cooperative

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Ownership)
(a) Public
(b) Private
(c) Joint
(d) Cooperative

List-II (Example)
(i) Amul
(ii) JSW
(iii) APIIC joint ventures
(iv) BHEL

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: BHEL is public sector, JSW is private sector, APIIC joint ventures belong to the joint sector, and Amul is cooperative.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive cooperative example and then verify the remaining ownership pairs.
accepted.sec: By ownership - public, private, joint, cooperative

accepted.s: Maruti Udyog was originally an example of which type of ownership?
o: Joint ownership between the Government of India and Suzuki
accepted.x: Maruti Udyog was originally a joint-sector undertaking involving the Government of India and Suzuki.
accepted.tq: Distinguish joint ownership from public and private ownership by identifying both partners.
accepted.sec: By ownership - public, private, joint, cooperative

accepted.s:
With reference to the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, consider the following statements:

1. Schedule A industries were reserved for the public sector.
2. Arms, atomic energy, and iron and steel were included in Schedule A.
3. Schedule B industries were open only to private enterprises.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Schedule A industries, including arms, atomic energy, and iron and steel, were reserved for the public sector. Schedule B industries were open to both public and private sectors, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Watch for the ownership trap created by the word ‘only’ in statement 3.
accepted.sec: By ownership - public, private, joint, cooperative

accepted.s: The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises was formed in 2007 by merging which two ministries?
o: Ministry of Rural Development and Ministry of Agriculture
Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industries
Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries
accepted.x: The Ministry of MSME was formed in 2007 by merging the Ministry of Small Scale Industries with the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact predecessor ministries rather than choosing similarly named ministries.
accepted.sec: By size and capital - large, medium, small, MSME

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the role of MSMEs in relation to large industries?
o: They function as complementary ancillary units
They are confined exclusively to agriculture
accepted.x: MSMEs complement large industries by functioning as ancillary units and supplying components or supporting services.
accepted.tq: Apply the complementary relationship between MSMEs and large industries.
accepted.sec: By size and capital - large, medium, small, MSME

accepted.s: The 2020 definition of MSMEs introduced which major change?
o: Classification exclusively by number of workers
A composite criterion of investment and turnover, without distinguishing manufacturing from services
accepted.x: The 2020 definition uses a composite criterion of investment and turnover and removes the earlier distinction between manufacturing and service enterprises.
accepted.tq: Identify the paired criteria and the specific distinction that was removed.
accepted.sec: By size and capital - large, medium, small, MSME

accepted.s: According to APSES 2024–25, how many large and mega industries were operational in Andhra Pradesh, and what employment did they represent?
accepted.x: APSES 2024–25 reported 1,074 operational large and mega industries, involving ₹3.01 lakh crore and 5.33 lakh jobs.
accepted.tq: Match the count with the correct employment figure before considering the investment figure.
accepted.sec: By size and capital - large, medium, small, MSME

accepted.s: Which one of the following is classified as a basic or primary good?
accepted.x: Steel, cement and coal are examples of basic or primary goods.
accepted.tq: Distinguish foundational industrial inputs from consumer and capital goods.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Use-based group)
(a) Capital goods
(b) Intermediate goods
(c) Consumer durables
(d) Consumer non-durables

List-II (Example)
(i) Food
(ii) Machinery
(iii) Chemicals
(iv) Appliances

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Machinery is a capital good, chemicals are intermediate goods, appliances are consumer durables, and food is a consumer non-durable.
accepted.tq: Classify each product according to its use and durability.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the use-based classes employed in the Index of Industrial Production?
accepted.x: The IIP use-based classes include primary, capital, intermediate, infrastructure/construction, consumer durables and consumer non-durables. Export goods is not one of the listed classes.
accepted.tq: Find the option that is not a use-based industrial classification.

accepted.s: The Second Five Year Plan, associated with the Mahalanobis model, gave particular emphasis to:
accepted.x: The Second Plan and the Mahalanobis model stressed the development of basic and heavy industries.
accepted.tq: Link the planning model with its characteristic industrial emphasis.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes heavy industries from light industries?
o: Heavy industries are always labour-intensive, whereas light industries are always capital-intensive
Heavy industries use bulky inputs and produce bulky outputs, whereas light industries generally use lighter inputs and produce consumer products
There is no difference between the two classifications
Heavy industries are confined to services, whereas light industries are confined to mining
accepted.x: Heavy industries are associated with bulky inputs and outputs and are generally capital-intensive. Light industries use lighter inputs and commonly produce consumer goods.
accepted.tq: Compare the input-output characteristics rather than the ownership of industries.

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of a heavy industry mentioned in relation to India?
accepted.x: Heavy Engineering Corporation at Ranchi is an example of heavy industry. Garments, electronics assembly and toys are lighter or manpower-based activities.
accepted.tq: Identify the capital-intensive heavy-industry example among consumer-oriented activities.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Sunrise industry — Green hydrogen
2. Sunrise industry — Electric vehicles
3. Sunset industry — Legacy print
4. Sunset industry — Thermal coal equipment

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Artificial intelligence, green hydrogen, electric vehicles and semiconductors are identified as sunrise areas, while legacy print and thermal coal equipment are sunset areas. All four listed pairs are correct.
accepted.tq: Separate emerging sunrise sectors from declining legacy sectors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a fuel-based industry?
accepted.x: Refineries, petrochemicals, thermal power and coal-gasification fertiliser units are fuel-based industries.
accepted.tq: Identify industries whose principal location or operation is linked to fuel inputs.

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with the MSE-Cluster Development Programme in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, 29 projects were approved under the MSE-Cluster Development Programme, of which 11 were completed.
accepted.tq: Keep approval and completion counts in their correct order.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a manpower-based industry or activity?
accepted.x: Handloom weaving, pottery and toy making are manpower-based activities. Oil refining is a fuel-based industry.
accepted.tq: Use the defining input of the industry to identify the exception.

accepted.s: An industry requiring skilled labour and reliable internet connectivity, but not proximity to bulky raw materials, is most likely to be classified as:
accepted.x: Footloose industries such as software, diamond polishing and electronics assembly are not tied to the location of raw materials and depend on skills and connectivity.
accepted.tq: Infer the industrial category from its location requirements.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following sectors in ascending order of the stage of economic activity:

A. Tertiary
B. Primary
C. Quaternary
D. Secondary

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The sector ladder proceeds from primary extraction to secondary manufacturing, tertiary services and quaternary knowledge, research and IT activities.
accepted.tq: Use the sector ladder from extraction to manufacturing, services and knowledge activities.

accepted.s: The term “gold collar” is associated with which sector?
o: Quaternary sector involving research and development
accepted.x: The quinary sector is described as the “gold collar” sector and involves top-level decision-making.
accepted.tq: Distinguish quinary decision-making from quaternary knowledge and R&D activities.

accepted.s: Under the old series with base year 2011–12, the eight core industries together accounted for what share of the Index of Industrial Production?
accepted.x: The eight core industries accounted for 40.27% of the IIP weight under the old series with base year 2011–12.
accepted.tq: Use the base-year qualifier to identify the correct aggregate weight.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct descending order of the weights of the three leading components of the old Index of Eight Core Industries?
accepted.x: Refinery products had the highest weight at 28.04%, followed by electricity at 19.85% and steel at 17.92%.
accepted.tq: Begin with the highest-weight component and compare the next two values.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its weight in the old Index of Eight Core Industries?
accepted.x: Coal had a weight of 10.33%. Crude oil, cement and fertilisers had weights of 8.98%, 5.37% and 2.63%, respectively.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical pair against the core-industry weight table.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: Which industry had the lowest weight in the old Index of Eight Core Industries?
accepted.x: Fertilisers had the lowest weight, at 2.63%, in the old eight-core-industry series.
accepted.tq: Identify the minimum value rather than the largest component.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s:
With reference to the revised Index of Core Industries series beginning with June 2026 data, consider the following statements:

1. Iron ore was added as a ninth sector.
2. Double-counting in steel and coal was removed.
3. The new base year and nine-sector weights are specified in the available information.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The revised series added iron ore, making nine sectors, and removed double-counting in steel and coal. The new base year and nine-sector weights are not specified here, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate the stated features of a revision from details that are not supplied.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: The growth of the Index of Eight Core Industries in July 2026 was:
accepted.x: The Index of Core Industries grew by 5.4% in July 2026, compared with 6% in June 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the July growth rate from the preceding month’s figure.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: Which pair correctly represents the growth rates reported for iron ore and coal in July 2026?
accepted.x: Iron ore recorded growth of 29.5%, while coal grew by 7.6% in July 2026.
accepted.tq: Match each sector with its own growth rate rather than the aggregate rate.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the tenth revision of the Index of Industrial Production is correct?

1. Its base year is 2022–23.
2. It covers 1,042 products in 463 item groups.
3. Manufacturing has a weight of 76.1%.
4. It is compiled by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The tenth IIP revision uses 2022–23 as base year, covers 1,042 products in 463 groups, assigns manufacturing a 76.1% weight, and is compiled by NSO under MoSPI.
accepted.tq: Verify the revision through its base year, coverage, weight and compiling authority.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the sectoral weights in the revised IIP?
o: Manufacturing 70.1%, mining 16.1%, electricity and gas 11.1%, water supply 2.63%
Manufacturing 76.1%, mining 11.1%, electricity and gas 10.9%, water supply 2.02%
Manufacturing 76.1%, mining 10.9%, electricity and gas 11.1%, water supply 2.02%
Manufacturing 75.1%, mining 12.1%, electricity and gas 10.9%, water supply 2.02%
accepted.x: The revised IIP weights are manufacturing 76.1%, mining 11.1%, electricity and gas 10.9%, and water supply 2.02%.
accepted.tq: Check the complete weight sequence, especially the close mining and electricity figures.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: The IIP recorded growth of 7.3% in June 2026. This was described as:
accepted.x: IIP growth of 7.3% in June 2026 was reported as a 23-month high.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a stated comparative high from an unsupported absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Core industries - Index of Eight Core Industries

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the Andhra Pradesh sector map?
o: Visakhapatnam—engineering and metallurgy; Nellore—leather, electronics and auto parts
Kurnool—textiles and ceramics; Visakhapatnam—food processing alone
Prakasam—marine processing alone; Anantapur—coal mining alone
accepted.x: The AP sector map identifies Visakhapatnam with engineering and metallurgy and Nellore with leather, electronics and auto parts. Other regions include West Godavari textiles and ceramics, Guntur food processing and cement, and Prakasam and Kurnool mineral-based industries.
accepted.tq: Match districts with their distinctive industrial clusters and reject reversed locations.

accepted.s: Which district-sector pair is NOT correctly matched in the Andhra Pradesh sector map?
accepted.x: Prakasam is associated with mineral-based industries, not leather and auto parts. Leather and auto parts are associated with Nellore.
accepted.tq: Use the district-specific industrial map to identify the swapped location.

accepted.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh campaign mentioned for August 2026, industries are required to plant trees on what proportion of their premises?
accepted.x: The campaign requires industries to plant trees on 33% of their premises.
accepted.tq: Recall the prescribed environmental proportion without converting it into a different percentage.
